body:
### Summary

I have a user-level `uv.toml` with shared settings in my configuration repo that I use across machines. However some settings are machine-dependent.

It doesn’t seem like one can split the user-level configuration into multiple files (into something like a `uv.toml.d` folder), correct me if I’m wrong.

While there are some ways to work around it (init scripts that set environment variables or create symlinks, or maybe use the system-level configuration as well on a single-user system), it feels like this is a common approach to config files that would make this task a lot easier.

### Example

```ascii
~/.config
└── uv
    ├── uv.toml
    └── uv.toml.d
        ├── 000-certificates.toml
        └── 001-indexes.toml
```

1. Files in `uv.toml.d` should be applied in lexicographical order, after the main `uv.toml`
2. Only files ending in `.toml` should be considered (this allows to switch between configs/templates more easily by suffixing them)
title: Allow user-level `uv.toml` to be split
